dave (ACME - infra): Hey team — started seeing a spike at ~09:20 UTC. US customers behind our on-prem peering are getting calls routed to Redwood EU region. Latency + auth failures: ~300-600ms extra and intermittent 401 on tokened endpoints.

alice (Support): Sorry you're hitting this, can you share a minimal repro request + any headers you see? Also a traceroute/tcpdump would help.

dave (ACME - infra): quick curl I ran from an edge VM in our colo (US-east):

```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_prod_xxx" 
  https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/generate 
  -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```

Response headers we got (server shows EU backend):
```
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 09:21:04 GMT
Content-Type: application/json
x-redwood-region: eu-west-1
x-request-id: rwd-abc123
```

dave (ACME - infra): traceroute from same VM shows hop to partner proxy in frankfurt before hitting internet egress IP:
```
1  10.0.0.1
2  192.168.100.1
3  185.24.12.34  (partner-proxy-frankfurt)
4  62.210.11.55  (to internet)
```

dave (ACME - infra): tcpdump on vm showing source NATed public IP is partner-owned (EU). So calls leave with EU public IP.

carlos (Infra): OK that explains routing. Redwood routing chooses serving region based on source IP geolocation (for Hosted/Shared routing we use client egress IP to pick nearest region). If your egress IP is in EU, our router picks EU pool.

alice (Support): That lines up with the x-redwood-region header in the response. Do you have a per-tenant region binding? Could explain 401s if tokens are region-scoped.

emily (Solutions): Quick note: for Dedicated/Private customers we normally allow regional pinning, but if requests originate from a different public IP we may still route by egress IP. The 401 could be because the token was issued for us-west-2 and EU pool rejects it.

infra-oncall (bot): Incident created: INC-20260311-042, assigned to carlos.

carlos (Infra): Two remediation paths:
1) Fix your egress so outbound connections use a US public IP (SNAT) that maps to a US location.
2) If using an HTTP proxy that terminates and re-originates requests, ensure it preserves original client IP via Proxy Protocol or X-Forwarded-For AND coordinate with Redwood support to trust that header for routing (we can enable region override for testing).

alice (Support): For immediate mitigation we can enable a temporary routing override on your tenant so all requests map to us-west-2, but this is not a long-term fix — better to fix egress. Want us to enable the override?

dave (ACME - infra): Would prefer a longer-term fix. But we need a short-term patch while we roll changes with our peering partner. Please enable override.

emily (Solutions): Done — I requested region override for tenant acme-123 to us-west-2. You should see lower latency in ~30s. Note: token validation checks will still happen against the chosen region, so existing tokens should now be accepted.

carlos (Infra): Can you share your NAT rules / iptables SNAT config? Typical misconfig is SNAT to the peer proxy IP range.

dave (ACME - infra): SNAT rule we currently have on our egress gateway (simplified):
```
iptables -t nat -A POSTROUTING -o eth0 -j SNAT --to-source 185.24.12.34
```

dave (ACME - infra): Partner proxy was added as a compliance passthrough and they SNAT everything to their EU IP. We're switching to a route that SNATs to our own US egress IP instead.

carlos (Infra): Right — change to SNAT to a US public IP that geolocates to your desired region. Alternatively, if you need partner proxy for auditing, ask them to preserve client IP (use X-Forwarded-For and avoid SNAT) or use Proxy Protocol/TCP passthrough.

alice (Support): After you change SNAT, can you post a quick curl with `-i` showing `x-redwood-region` in the response? We'll confirm routing back to us-west.

dave (ACME - infra): Making change now. Will report back in ~10m.

(10 minutes later)

dave (ACME - infra): Updated. New tcpdump shows egress IP is 54.245.66.12 (US). Re-ran curl:
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 09:33:07 GMT
Content-Type: application/json
x-redwood-region: us-west-2
x-request-id: rwd-xyz789
```

dave (ACME - infra): Latency back to normal ~35ms, no more 401s. Thanks.

emily (Solutions): Great. For long term we recommend one of:
- Terminate proxy in transparent mode or preserve X-Forwarded-For and coordinate with us to trust it for routing
- Ensure egress SNAT maps to the intended region's public IP block
- If you require partner egress through EU, request regional pinning on your tenant and use a dedicated cross-region routing config (we can help architect).

carlos (Infra): I'm going to add a note to our runbook: "Private/VPC egress via third-party proxies can change perceived client region — confirm public egress IP geolocation matches desired Redwood region or preserve original client IP via proxy protocol."

alice (Support): Closing loop here. Please reopen if anything resurfaces. :thumbsup:

dave (ACME - infra): Thanks all. We'll update partner and document the SNAT change in our change log.
